newsitem.title: USA: Freight train crashes in Virginia, one person hurt.
newsitem.headline: Freight train crashes in Virginia, one person hurt.

text.p: A freight train jumped the track Friday and crashed into a gas station bathroom in Gainesville, Va., injuring one person and spilling 3,000 gallons of diesel fuel, an emergency services spokesman said.
Three engines and four piggyback freight cars careened off the track, Tom Hajduk, deputy co-ordinator for emergency services in Prince William County, said.
"In the process of coming off the track, the train crushed several automobiles and a restroom building at a race track gas station," Hajduk said.
The cars had been parked by the gas station in Gainesville, which is about eight miles northwest of Manassas.
The injured person was taken by helicopter to a hospital and the extent of the injuries was not known, Hajduk said.
The fuel leak was contained and roads around the crash site reopened, he said. The cause of the accident was unknown.
Hajduk said the freight cars were "piggyback" type cars like the ones used to carry automobiles but he did not know what they were transporting at the time of the crash.
